extracted.intended_audience: policy makers, national/regional IP office staff, statisticians and researchers using WIPO intellectual property statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and metrics for compiling, counting and interpreting WIPO plant variety (and related office procedural) statistics, including definitions (office vs origin), count methods (absolute vs equivalent), table metrics (applications processed, registered, rejected, etc.), and cautions on comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table procedural metrics (industrial design / plant variety)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table columns used to report office procedural data: Total applications processed; Registered; Rejected; Withdrawn or abandoned; Applications pending; Number of examiners (FTE); First office action from filing date (days); Final office decision from filing date (days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the standard metrics reported per office in the procedural tables. FTE is defined as full time equivalent (see separate note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of examiners (FTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of examiners reported on a full time equivalent (FTE) basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: FTE is full time equivalent. This metric standardizes staff counts across offices regardless of part-time/contract arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: First office action from filing date (days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time (in days) from filing date to first office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported per office as an indicator of examination responsiveness; procedural differences between offices can affect comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final office decision from filing date (days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time (in days) from filing date to a final office decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure total processing time to decision; delays in procedures and capacity affect this metric and cross-office comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs non‑resident (office data vs origin data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction: applications received by offices from resident and non-resident applicants are referred to as office data; applications filed by applicants at a national or regional office (resident applications) or at a foreign office (applications abroad) are referred to as origin data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For EU-domiciled applicants, filing at the CPVO regional office is regarded as a resident filing. Users should be careful to choose the appropriate data view (office vs origin) for their analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Counting method where an application received by a regional office is counted only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute counts treat a regional-office filing as a single application regardless of the number of member states; used in some figures and tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Counting method where a single application filed at a regional office is treated as multiple equivalent applications (multiplied by the number of member states).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for CPVO applications, if the applicant resides in one of the 27 EU member states the application is counted as one resident filing and 26 filings abroad; if the applicant does not reside in an EU member state the application is counted as 27 filings abroad. Equivalent counts inflate regional-filed applications to reflect potential protection in multiple member states; expect European origins to move up in rankings under equivalent counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent/absolute count ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric showing the ratio between equivalent and absolute counts for filings or titles issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to illustrate the amplification effect of equivalent counting for origins with intensive regional-office filings; helps interpret differences between absolute and equivalent rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage and world totals caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: World totals and regional totals are WIPO estimates based on a subset of offices (e.g., 'World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering 72 offices' or similar notes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should note the number of offices covered when interpreting world/regional totals; not all offices are included in every estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability caution across offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural differences across offices make it difficult to fully harmonize data; caution is advised when making comparisons across offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The total number of applications processed for any given office may be incomplete due to omission of elements by the office. Differences in procedures, definitions and capacity can bias cross-office comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities‑only data footnote
rubrics_metrics.description: Some reported data may refer to formalities examinations only (footnote '(a) data are for formalities examinations only').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When present, this limits comparability with offices reporting substantive examination statistics—analysts must account for this scope difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time‑lag caveat between applications and titles issued
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure for issuing titles varies across offices; examination capacity and procedural delays mean there are differences in the time lag between application and title issue dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this reason, data on applications for any given year should not be compared with data on titles issued that same year. Fluctuations in titles granted may reflect processing capacity and delays rather than substantive changes in filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of growth and regional shares
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on reading growth rates and regional shares (e.g., that increases/decreases in filings may be driven by resident vs non‑resident filings, transfers between regional and national offices, or one-off administrative events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the report: UK's surge in filings partly due to pending CPVO applications opting into the UK; China growth driven almost entirely by resident filings. Analysts should examine resident vs non-resident contributions to growth for proper attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of figures and tables with notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures and tables include specific notes (e.g., 'Note: CPVO is the Community Plant Variety Office of the European Union') and methodological footnotes that affect interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always read figure/table notes and the glossary/methodology when using the numbers. Regional office labels, member counts, and special-case treatments (such as CPVO counting) are documented in notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'titles in force' and issuance counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of plant variety titles issued and titles in force are reported separately and can fluctuate due to processing time; titles in force are the active protections at year-end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes in the number of titles issued in a year do not directly equate to changes in titles in force; analysts should use 'titles in force' for active-protection stock and 'titles issued' for flow, accounting for timing differences.
